sections.text:
In the warm summer, the fields were bustling with life, and the sun was shining brightly, illuminating the flowers and warming the insects.

There was a green grasshopper (grasshopper) who spent his days jumping among the tall grass, singing loudly, and playing his little violin, enjoying his time without any worry or care.

Nearby, there was a small, very active ant, working hard from sunrise until sunset.

The ant was carrying heavy grains of wheat and large pieces of corn, several times its weight, and dragging them with great difficulty towards its underground colony for storage.

The lazy grasshopper saw her sweating from fatigue, so he laughed at her and said sarcastically: “You poor ant! Why do you bother yourself with such hard work in this beautiful weather? Come play and sing with me!”

The ant paused for a moment to wipe the sweat from her forehead, and said in a serious voice: “I am collecting food and storing it for the coming harsh winter, and I advise you to do the same before it is too late.”

The grasshopper laughed louder and said: “Winter?! Winter is still so far away! We have so much food everywhere now, why should we worry about the future?”

The wise ant ignored him and went back to her hard work, while the grasshopper continued to play and sing throughout the summer and fall days.

The days passed quickly, the seasons changed, the cold and dark winter arrived, and heavy snow fell, covering the fields and trees with its icy white coat.

All the flowers died, the green grass was gone, and there was no longer any food available on the surface of the earth.

The ant and her family were sitting in their warm underground colony, eating from the abundant food that the energetic ant had stored up all summer, and they were happy and comfortable.

As for the lazy grasshopper, he was shivering from the cold and starved for several days until his body was completely weak and he was no longer able to jump or sing.

The grasshopper remembered his neighbor, the ant, so he went, dragging his feet with difficulty through the snow until he reached the door of her house and knocked on the door weakly.

The ant opened the door and saw the grasshopper in a miserable state. He said to her in a trembling voice: “Please, my friend the ant, give me one grain of wheat to live, for I am dying of hunger and cold!”

The ant looked at him sadly and said: “What have you been doing all the long summer? Weren’t you collecting food as I advised you?”

The grasshopper hung his head in shame and said, “I was busy singing, playing, and enjoying myself, and I didn’t think about tomorrow.”

The ant sighed and said firmly: “He who sings and plays in the summer must dance from cold and hunger in the winter! This is the punishment for laziness and not planning for the future.”

The ant closed its door, leaving the lazy grasshopper to face his fate in the bitter cold, learning (albeit too late) that hard work in times of prosperity is the only guarantee of survival in times of hardship.
